title: Four-Round HadesMiMC Truncated Differential Security
summary: The source finds no probability-one trail beyond one round but leaves longer trails unexcluded, so the four-round security conjecture remains open.

formal_statement.body: The possibility of longer truncated differential trails has not been excluded, whether or not they depend on details of the S-box. Prove or refute the conjecture that four rounds of HadesMiMC with full S-box layers are secure against truncated differential attacks.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of HadesMiMC using truncated differential attacks.
parameters: Four rounds, the target reduced-round setting
Full S-box layers, the specified round configuration
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether longer truncated differential trails can be set up, whether or not they depend on details of the S-box, and prove or refute the conjecture that four rounds of HadesMiMC with full S-box layers are secure against truncated differential attacks.

citations.label: On a Generalization of Substitution-Permutation Networks: The HADES Design Strategy

progress.summary: The source presents this as an explicit conjecture after comparing HadesMiMC's full-state diffusion with AES. It notes that longer truncated differential trails have not been excluded and asks whether four rounds are secure.
citation_labels: Lorenzo Grassi et al., On a Generalization of Substitution-Permutation Networks: The HADES Design Strategy
